sites.accuracy: 2/3 fields exact match; 1/3 field (username_placeholder) returned null instead of 'Username'
sites.root_cause_investigation: Called webaccess.tier2_rendered.render() directly on this URL to inspect what content the LLM actually received. page.aria (accessibility snapshot) DOES contain the placeholder as the textbox's accessible name: 'textbox "Username"' -- full aria snapshot is only 34 words. router._llm_from_rendered() uses `content = page.aria if len(page.aria.split()) > 50 else page.text`. Because 34 < 50, it falls back to page.text, which is only 3 words ('Welcome\nView Cards') and does NOT include the placeholder (placeholders are DOM attributes, not text nodes, so they never appear in visible innerText). The LLM therefore never saw the placeholder value and correctly returned null for a field it had no evidence for -- this is not an LLM hallucination, it is the router's word-count fallback threshold discarding the one representation (aria) that actually had the answer, on small/sparse SPA screens.
sites.validator_note: task still reported success=true because validate_fields only requires >=1 of the requested fields to be present/non-empty; 2 of 3 fields were present.

summary_observations: All 3 SPA/CSR sites correctly skip the static-HTML LLM tier: looks_like_js_shell() (visible body words < 60 after stripping <script>/<style>) triggers on every one, so tier1 static_llm is never attempted, and tier2 rendered_llm succeeds on the first try (haiku) every time.

quotes.toscrape.com/js/ is a good adversarial case for JS-shell detection specifically because the data is present in the raw HTML text (inside a <script> tag) but not as visible text -- confirming the shell detector is checking rendered visibility, not raw byte presence.

Found one real parser bug: router._llm_from_rendered()'s `len(page.aria.split()) > 50` threshold silently drops the accessibility-tree snapshot in favor of plain innerText on short/sparse pages, even when the aria snapshot contains information (e.g. input placeholders exposed as accessible names) that plain text never carries. Reproduced on rickandmortyapi-react.netlify.app (aria=34 words, text=3 words); the missing 'username_placeholder' field is a direct consequence, not an LLM hallucination.

Cache replay works correctly (method suffixed '(cached)', discovery ladder skipped, identical data returned) but for pages that already succeed on the very first Tier-2 attempt, caching provides no measurable latency win: 3 measurements averaged ~7.9s uncached vs ~10.8s cached, i.e. slower on average, purely due to Playwright render / Anthropic API call-latency noise dominating the (already tiny) discovery overhead being saved.
